source.title: Conway, Algebraic Concordance and Casson-Gordon Invariants lecture notes

source_resolution.reason: The Conway notes are retrieved and relevant; Lemma 2.31 supplies a complete local zero-surgery splitting proof. Theorem 2.33 states prime-power tau vanishing, and Casson–Gordon (1986), Theorem 2, gives a disk-exterior proof route. The latter still relies on bounding-pair independence and bordism inputs not fully derived in the inspected chapter; the Ω3 computation is also invoked without proof. The remaining owner escalation is mathematical; no source is dropped.
source_resolution.search_summary: The original unige route redirected and a course-resource Google Drive copy returned Cache miss. A timestamped Internet Archive snapshot was then successfully retrieved. Lemma 2.31 is now proved locally. Theorem 2.33 states the exact prime-power vanishing interface but explicitly defers its proof to Casson–Gordon (1975), Theorem 2; Lemma 2.32 refers twisted-form nonsingularity to that source. The remaining owner escalation is mathematical, not a failed retrieval. A primary 1986 chapter was also retrieved and read through Theorem 2. It supplies the disk-exterior vanishing route and special twisted-homology argument, but its τ-independence and Ω3-finiteness inputs are stated or referred to earlier results rather than proved completely. The 1986 primary chapter was retrieved and read through Theorem 2. It proves the disk-exterior tau-vanishing route, but its proof assumes tau bounding-pair independence and invokes an Ω3 finiteness result without proving the full computation; the remaining escalations are mathematical.

alternatives.argument: A complete local mod-p cyclic-cover argument is supplied from deck-chain exact sequences and Frobenius.
The local proof attaches the branched disk model, identifies the overlap generator, applies Mayer–Vietoris, and rationalizes by finite CW type.
The boundary kernel proof is supplied using the homology-pair sequence, Poincaré–Lefschetz duality, UCT, and the Bockstein linking form.

The primary 1986 Theorem 2 and proof give the exact slice-disk τ-vanishing route, including the disk-induced kernel and character extension. The argument assumes τ is well-defined independently of its bounding pair; that prerequisite is not fully established in the inspected treatment, so no complete local proof is claimed.
The full contrapositive is drafted, but the contradiction depends on the escalated signature-vanishing claim.
